concepts.title: Antiderivative and the Indefinite Integral
concepts.definition: Given a function f, any function F whose derivative equals f is an antiderivative of f; the whole family F(x) + C, with C an arbitrary real constant, is written as the indefinite integral of f with respect to x.
concepts.formula: integral(f(x)) dx = F(x) + C where d/dx of F(x) = f(x)
concepts.key_idea: Integrating reverses differentiating, but only up to an added constant.

concepts.title: Standard Integration Formulae from the Derivative Table
concepts.definition: Each differentiation rule read backwards produces a ready-made integral: the power rule lifts the exponent by one and divides by it, the exponential integrates to itself, reciprocal x gives the log, and each trig function pairs with a listed primitive.
concepts.formula: integral(x**n) dx = x**(n + 1)/(n + 1) + C valid for n other than -1
concepts.key_idea: The derivative table converts directly into a table of standard integrals.

concepts.title: Linearity Properties of the Indefinite Integral
concepts.definition: Integrals respect sums and constant multiples: an integral of a sum splits into separate integrals, a constant factor moves outside the integral sign, and differentiating an integral hands back the original integrand.
concepts.formula: integral(k1*f1(x) + k2*f2(x)) dx = k1*integral(f1(x)) dx + k2*integral(f2(x)) dx
concepts.key_idea: Split sums, pull constants out, and always verify by differentiating the answer.

concepts.title: Integration by Substitution
concepts.definition: When the integrand contains a function together with a multiple of its derivative, renaming that inner function as a new variable t rewrites both the integrand and the differential, turning the problem into a simpler standard integral in t.
concepts.formula: integral(f(x)) dx with x = g(t) becomes integral(f(g(t)) * g_prime(t)) dt
concepts.key_idea: Spot an inner function whose derivative also appears in the integrand, then switch variables.

solution_steps.action: Choose the inner function whose derivative occurs in the integrand
solution_steps.explain: Typical choices are the argument of a trig or exponential term.

solution_steps.explain: If t equals the inner function, dt carries the missing derivative factor.

concepts.title: Logarithmic Integrals of tan, cot, sec and cosec
concepts.definition: Four recurring trig integrals end in logarithms: tangent gives log of secant, cotangent gives log of sine, secant gives log of the sum secant plus tangent, and cosecant gives log of cosecant minus cotangent, each reached by a clever factor times substitution.
concepts.key_idea: Tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant each integrate to a logarithm of a trig expression.

concepts.title: Integration Using Trigonometric Identities
concepts.definition: Powers and products of sine and cosine are integrated by first rewriting them with identities, such as the half-angle formula for squared terms and the product-to-sum formula for mixed products, which reduces the integrand to first-power trig terms.
concepts.key_idea: Lower the powers and split the products with identities before integrating.

concepts.title: Standard Forms with Quadratic Denominators
concepts.definition: Integrals built from x squared plus or minus a squared have fixed primitives: reciprocal of x squared plus a squared gives an arctangent, reciprocal of a squared minus x squared gives a logarithm, and reciprocal of the square root of a squared minus x squared gives an arcsine; completing the square reduces harder quadratics to these shapes.

concepts.title: Integration by Partial Fractions
concepts.definition: A proper rational function, a polynomial ratio whose numerator degree is below the denominator degree, splits into simpler fractions, one per distinct factor of the denominator with extra terms for repeated factors; each piece then integrates by known rules.
concepts.formula: integral(p(x)/((x - a)*(x - b))) dx = A*log(x - a) + B*log(x - b) + C
concepts.key_idea: Factor the denominator, split into partial fractions, integrate the simple pieces.

concepts.title: Integration by Parts and the ILATE Choice
concepts.definition: For a product of two unlike functions, integration by parts shifts the difficulty from one factor to the other: the product rule integrated gives first times integral of second, minus the integral of derivative of first times integral of second. The ILATE ordering picks which factor differentiates.
concepts.formula: integral(f(x) * g(x)) dx = f(x) * integral(g(x)) dx - integral(f_prime(x) * V(x)) dx where V = integral(g(x)) dx
concepts.key_idea: Choose the first function by ILATE so the remaining integral is easier than the original.

concepts.title: Exponential Pattern of e to the x times Function plus Its Derivative
concepts.definition: An integrand of the form the exponential times a bracket containing a function and its own derivative integrates directly to the exponential times the function, a pattern worth spotting before attempting parts.
concepts.formula: integral(e**x * (f(x) + f_prime(x))) dx = e**x * f(x) + C
concepts.key_idea: When the bracket is a function plus its derivative, the answer is the exponential times the function.

concepts.title: Evaluating a Definite Integral by the Fundamental Theorem
concepts.definition: For an integrand continuous between the limits, the definite integral equals any antiderivative at the upper limit minus the same antiderivative at the lower limit; the constant of integration cancels and never appears.
concepts.formula: integral from lower to upper of f(x) dx = F(upper) - F(lower) where F is an antiderivative of f
concepts.key_idea: Find the antiderivative once, then subtract its values at the two limits.

solution_steps.explain: The primitive of slope*x + intercept is slope*x**2/2 + intercept*x.

solution_steps.action: Evaluate the same antiderivative at the lower limit
solution_steps.explain: Substituting the lower limit gives the value to subtract.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the lower value from the upper value
solution_steps.explain: By the second fundamental theorem this difference is the definite integral.

concepts.title: Properties of Definite Integrals Including the King Property
concepts.definition: Definite integrals obey structural rules: interchanging the limits flips the sign, an integral splits at an interior point into two integrals, replacing x by the sum of the limits minus x leaves the value unchanged, and symmetric limits collapse to zero for odd integrands.
concepts.formula: integral from 0 to a of f(x) dx = integral from 0 to a of f(a - x) dx
concepts.key_idea: Swap, split or reflect the limits to simplify a definite integral before computing it.
